event: For a while nobody moves.
Then Astra moves away, up out of the overlap, and the cool where she was is instant.
She sits back on her heels at the fort's mouth, every motion exactly where she means it.
"Where are you going," Nova mumbles, eyes still shut.
"The shelf." Astra is already up: neither of you is to move.
She's built up to this for three days and will lose her nerve if you're helpful.
You prop up on your elbows to watch her cross the room.
A small pale thing has sat on that shelf at eye level for days; you'd half-clocked it.
She reaches it and stops, back to you, hands loose, looking at it.
She picks it up and turns.
She comes back with both hands cupped round something you can't see yet.
She folds down into the fort with more care than the trip needs.
She opens her hands over the blanket between the three of you.
It's a leaf: a single sheet thin as paper and not paper, pale, faintly lit from inside.
Its edges don't quite hold still when you look straight at them.
When Astra breathes, it stirs.
You sit up to see it.
"It's a page of the first stuff," she says.
The material everything's made of before it's made into anything; there's little of it.
"This is a piece of mine."
Nova comes up on both elbows, red eyes huge, and her words don't arrive.
Astra: it holds what you put on it, not for a long time but forever, the real one.
She sets an ordinary ballpoint pen on the blanket beside it; your eye goes to the pen.
It's blank: she didn't want to be the one who decided what it says.
Nova reaches for it slowly, both hands, as if it might be hot, and stops short. "Can I."
"You can hold it. It won't tear."
She lifts it onto her two palms; the appraisal she always has ready doesn't come.
"Okay," quietly, to the leaf: "This is the best thing I've ever held."
"Nova. Put it down." A beat. "Not away. Down."
Nova sets the leaf on the blanket and looks up; now you both look at Astra.
She has handed the credit off a hundred times; you watch her decline to now.
She holds where she is and takes the looking.
The glow comes up under her skin, and this time she does nothing to catch it.
It rises past hiding, its pale reaching your faces, her eyes on you the whole way.
She didn't leave it on the shelf for want of words, she says, slower now.
She left it to see if either of you would ask what it was.
"You didn't. You walked past it eleven times. I counted."
She wasn't hurt; she was interested in whether she could ask anyway.
Nova makes a low sound and comes up off her elbows, already moving.
"Wait," Astra says, not sharp; Nova waits, strung tight with it.
"Look at me. Not the thing I made. Me."
For one night she'd like to be the thing picked up, not the thing everything's set on.
Your eyes went to her before she finished, and haven't come back.
The hard part: she asked aloud, so the answer has to come aloud.
"Yeah," you say, level, no performance: "I see you."
You tell her she's lit up like something struck and holding her face like she meant it.
You stop before finishing, so as not to hand her a joke to hide behind.
"I see you. That's the answer. I'm not looking at the page."
Astra goes completely still; the glow answers for her, steady, full, unhidden.

memory.fact: Astra's stillness comes with a glow.

event: She looks at Nova, shaking on both hands where she was told to hold.
"Okay," Astra says, her voice not steady. "Okay. Now."
Nova hits the two of you like weather.
